messages:
maria: Heads-up — I'm proposing we coalesce user_route + route_metrics into a single analytics_entity table to reduce joins for the console dashboards. Draft PR incoming.

own: What's the main motivation? query perf on big tenants?

maria: Exactly. Dashboards p99 queries for route charts are doing multi-join scans on high-cardinality route sets. Coalescing will let us serve the time-series from one partitioned table and simplify rollups. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

tess: Concern: schema change will require a backfill for ~300M rows. How do we avoid saturating PG and blocking writes?

maria: Plan A: dual-write for 2 weeks with a background backfill job throttled by tokens. Plan B (fallback): keep current schema and add a materialized view for most-used routes.

ashok: Dual-write + shadow read during canary sounds good. Make sure writes are idempotent — use route_id + ingestion_bucket as natural key.

own: For the backfill, can we do chunked copying using route shards and per-tenant windowing so the job can be paused?

maria: Yes. Backfill job will be sharded by tenant_group and time-window. We'll also expose a 'backfill-rate' gauge in console so SRE can throttle.

tess: Add a safety gate: if console p99 or PG load > 0.7, auto-throttle or pause backfill. Also require a manual ops signoff for large tenants.

schema-bot: NOTE: PR 4721 created by maria links to migration plan: https://git.internal/redwood/PR/4721 — contains backfill job and feature flag gating.

ashok: What about queries that currently rely on route_metrics being denormalized? We'll need read adapters for older UI endpoints during cutover.

maria: We'll ship a thin read adapter in the console service that queries analytics_entity when FF=on, otherwise falls back. No UI changes expected.

own: Can we run a small canary on non-paid tenants first for ~48hrs? If metrics match within epsilon, progressively increase coverage.

tess: Also plan for quick rollback: if we detect metric deltas > 2% on core KPIs, flip the FF off and stop writes to the new table. Must be automated.

maria: Agreed. We'll add a regression monitor: compare aggregate token counts and latency metrics between old and new pipelines. Thresholds configurable.

schema-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary: 5012350000 — canary window 2h.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started to eng-canary cluster.

own: Post-migration query compatibility checklist? indexing, partitioning, retention TTLs, and compacted materialized aggregates.

maria: Draft checklist: 1) index parity 2) partitioning by route_day 3) retention rewrite job 4) idempotent writes 5) monitoring hooks 6) rollback playbook. I'll add to PR.

ashok: One more: ensure we don't blow up our observability metrics cardinality — prefer sampled route tags for internal dashboards.

tess: Ack. Add an aggregation tier for high-cardinality tags and sample the detail stream to a logging bucket only.

maria: I'll schedule a short sync with SRE tomorrow 10:30 PT to walk through throttles and playbook. If no objections, I'll merge the PR in Friday canary window.

own: LGTM from me, please add explicit TTL on backfill job state so aborted runs don't accumulate.

maria: Will do. Thanks all.

deploy-bot: canary completed — no alerts in 2h window.

schema-bot: MIGRATION NOTE: Next step after canary is staged ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over 7 days. See PR for step timers and rollback thresholds.
